absent: Full fields and lifecycle of device private state and queue records beyond referenced members.
Transport semantics and completion handling of control command submission.
Queue resize helper behavior including memory handling and restart effects.
Steering commit and distribution update effects on hardware state.
Queue count update behavior and failure modes during channel changes.
Cleanup helper effects when affiliation setup fails or processors go offline.
Locking rules for steering, statistics, and coalescing state outside the shown guards.

findings.text: Affiliation refresh distributes currently online processors across the active queue pair count in similarly sized groups, with any remainder favoring early pairs. Both directions of a pair share one group, and completion records that hints are established.

Processor lifecycle callbacks adapt affiliation state for the instance linked from the notification node. Activation and termination recompute distribution, while preparation for removal clears affiliation. Each reports success.

Instance notification registration attaches one handle to a driver online state and another to a dead state without immediate callbacks. Failure of the second attachment undoes the first before propagating the error. Removal detaches both handles.

Per queue moderation programming submits a small host request carrying queue identity plus time and packet limits in host to device byte order through the coalescing control path. Receive and transmit wrappers require a negotiated moderation feature and cache programmed limits in the corresponding queue record on success.
Ring parameter query reports device maxima from first queue descriptors and current depths from the live ring size accessor for both directions.

Ring resize contract rejects mini and jumbo requests, treats an unchanged depth pair as success, and enforces per direction maxima. Changed directions are resized across every configured pair with stored moderation values reapplied afterwards. Unsupported moderation is tolerated while other failures abort.
Receive moderation reprogramming during receive resize is serialized by the per queue moderation guard, held across the reprogram operation and released before result checking.
Channel count update holds the processor set read guard across queue count change and affiliation refresh, releasing it on both success and failure paths.

Default steering initialization enables all supported hash kinds, derives an indirection mask from table size with empty table yielding zero, selects queue zero for unclassified traffic, refreshes distribution for the current pair count, and installs freshly generated key material with recorded length.

Hash field query maps transport over IP family flow kinds to address and transport selector indications derived from saved capabilities, preferring combined transport plus network coverage when available and falling back to network only. Unknown flow kinds yield no selectors and the operation always succeeds.

Hash field update accepts only address pair selection, address pair plus transport selectors, or discard. It clears prior bits for the addressed family, installs new bits unless discarding, rejects results outside supported capabilities or unknown flow kinds, and publishes plus conditionally commits changed sets when receive hashing is active.
Driver information reports module identity, driver version, and transport bus name. Bus naming falls back to a generic virtio label when the transport provides no naming callback.

Channel configuration supports only combined counts and rejects separate receive, transmit, or other counts, out of range or zero values, and changes while packet programs are attached. Successful changes update queue count, refresh affiliation, and publish new real queue counts.

Statistic name emission selects groups by control, receive, or transmit category and by whether a specific queue is addressed. Driver owned groups are always emitted while hardware groups require the matching device capability, using distinct plain and hardware qualified naming families.

Statistics context aggregates a destination selector between queue statistics and legacy output, per category descriptor counts, per category supported type bitmaps, per category reply size accumulation, and an output pointer. Three slots cover control, receive, and transmit categories.

Context initialization starts from base driver descriptor counts then adds capability gated hardware groups with matching bitmap flags, descriptor contributions, and reply byte contributions. Queue statistics mode and legacy mode use different base tables and different hardware subsets, with legacy mode additionally accounting for control queue statistics.
When processor set allocation fails, affiliation refresh abandons distribution and invokes cleanup without marking hints established, so callers must not assume hints exist after that path.
Pairs are resized sequentially with early exit on error, so a late failure can leave some pairs at new depths and others at old depths. The transition is not atomic across all pairs.
Notification coalescing uses a dedicated control class with a per queue set subcommand, exchanging queue identifier, time limit, and packet limit fields in little endian order.

Device statistics capabilities are individual type bits for control queue, receive basic, checksum, aggregation, rate, and transmit basic, checksum, aggregation, rate families that gate emitted and accounted hardware statistic groups.
